info.title: Entities API
info.description:
The Entities API provides full lifecycle management for entity records (profiles) in Reltio MDM. Entities are the core data objects — each entity represents a real-world business object such as a Person, Organization, Product, or Location.

Every entity belongs to exactly one entity type (defined in the tenant configuration) and contains: attributes (simple and nested values contributed by source systems), crosswalks (source-specific record identifiers that link back to originating systems), and operational metadata (creation time, update time, tags).

When multiple source systems contribute data for the same real-world object, Reltio's matching engine detects duplicates and merges them into a single golden record. The golden record's attribute values are determined by survivorship rules — configurable strategies that pick the best value from competing sources based on recency, frequency, source priority, or other criteria.

This API covers creating, reading, updating, deleting, and searching entity profiles, as well as specialized operations like Search Before Create (conditional upsert), key-based pagination, predicate queries, and on-the-fly data cleansing.

environment.description: Reltio environment name (e.g. dev, qa, prod)

post.description:
Creates one or more new entity profiles in the tenant. The request body is a JSON array of entity objects, each specifying a type and attributes. For each entity, at least one crosswalk must be provided to establish the source system linkage.

If matching is enabled for the entity type, the platform automatically evaluates match rules after creation. Newly created entities that match existing entities may be auto-merged depending on the match configuration (auto-merge vs. manual review).

Returns the created entity URIs in the response. For bulk creation, all entities in the array are processed as a single transaction.

200.description: Entities created successfully. Returns an array of created entity URIs.

400.description: Bad Request — the request body does not conform to the entity schema, or references an undefined entity type, attribute, or source.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to create entities in this tenant.

get.description:
Retrieves a list of entities from the tenant, optionally filtered by query parameters. Without filters, returns the most recently updated entities (paginated).

Common query parameters include `filter` (Reltio Query Language expression), `q` (full-text search), `type` (entity type URI), `options` (response shaping flags like `partialOverrides`, `crosswalks`, `score`), `offset` and `max` for pagination.

**Reltio Query Language (RQL)** supports attribute-based filtering with operators like `equals`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `nested`, `range`, and logical combinators (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`). Example: `filter=(equals(attributes.FirstName,'John') AND contains(attributes.LastName,'Smi'))`.

**Full-text search** via `q` parameter performs fuzzy matching across all indexed attributes with relevance scoring.

200.description: A JSON array of entity objects matching the query.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to read entities in this tenant.

delete.description:
Deletes entities from the tenant. The entities to delete are specified via query parameters — typically a filter expression or a list of entity URIs.

**Warning:** This operation is irreversible. Deleted entities and all their crosswalks, attributes, and relations are permanently removed. In production environments, consider using crosswalk end-dating instead of hard deletion to maintain audit trails.

200.description: Entities deleted successfully.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to delete entities in this tenant.

get.description:
Retrieves a single entity profile by its URI. The response includes all attributes (golden record values resolved by survivorship rules), crosswalks (source-specific identifiers), and operational metadata.

Use the `options` query parameter to control what's included in the response:
- `partialOverrides` — include attribute-level overrides from individual crosswalks
- `crosswalks` — include full crosswalk details
- `score` — include match/merge scores
- `history` — include change history

The entity URI format is `entities/{entityId}` where entityId is a platform-generated unique identifier.

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description: The unique entity identifier (the numeric or alphanumeric ID portion of the entity URI).

200.description: The full entity profile.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to read this entity.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified URI.

post.description:
Updates an existing entity profile by applying one or more changes. Unlike PUT (full replacement), this endpoint supports partial updates — you send only the attributes and crosswalks that need to change.

The update is applied as an upsert at the attribute level: existing attributes matching by crosswalk+name are updated; new attributes are added. The platform re-evaluates survivorship rules after the update to recalculate golden record values.

If the update changes match-relevant attributes, the matching engine is re-triggered and may detect new potential matches or cause auto-merges.

200.description: Entity updated successfully. Returns the updated entity.

400.description: Bad Request — the update body references undefined attributes or sources.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to update this entity.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified URI.

post.description:
Search Before Create (also known as conditional upsert) — the recommended approach for ingesting data into Reltio. Instead of blindly creating a new entity, this endpoint first searches for existing entities that match the incoming record based on the tenant's match rules.

Behavior depends on the match result:
- **No match found** — a new entity is created with the provided data.
- **Single match found** — the existing entity is updated with the new crosswalk and attribute values (upsert).
- **Multiple matches found** — the incoming data is merged into the best-matching entity; other matches may become potential matches for manual review.

This is the primary data ingestion endpoint for production ETL pipelines and real-time integrations because it prevents duplicate creation while maintaining data freshness.

200.description: Operation completed successfully. Returns the URIs of created or updated entities.

400.description: Bad Request — the request body does not conform to the entity schema.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to create or update entities in this tenant.

post.description:
Deletes entities specified in the request body. This POST variant is useful when the list of entity URIs to delete exceeds URL length limits for the DELETE method.

Accepts a JSON object with a `uris` array containing the entity URIs to delete. All specified entities are deleted in a single operation.

200.description: Entities deleted successfully.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

403.description: Forbidden — the caller does not have permission to delete entities in this tenant.

post.description:
Creates a deep copy of an existing entity profile, including all its attributes and optionally its crosswalks. The cloned entity receives a new URI and is independent from the original — subsequent changes to either entity do not affect the other.

Cloning is useful for creating template entities, testing data model changes, or splitting an incorrectly merged entity into separate records.

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description: The unique entity identifier of the entity to clone.

200.description: Entity cloned successfully. Returns the new entity URI.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified URI.

get.description:
Retrieves entities that contain a crosswalk matching the specified value. Crosswalks are source-specific record identifiers (e.g., CRM ID, ERP customer number) that link Reltio entities back to their originating source systems.

This endpoint is the primary way external systems look up their own records in Reltio — pass the source system's record ID and get back the Reltio golden record that contains it.

The crosswalk value is typically in the format `type/source/value` (e.g., `configuration/entityTypes/Person/CRM/12345`).

parameters.name: crosswalkValue
parameters.description: The crosswalk value to look up. Format depends on the crosswalk type configured for the entity type.

200.description: Entities containing the specified crosswalk.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

404.description: Not Found — no entity contains a crosswalk with the specified value.

get.description:
Retrieves an entity by its Reltio ID — a human-readable, auto-generated identifier that is unique within the tenant. Unlike the entity URI (which is an internal platform identifier), the Reltio ID is designed for external reference and can be configured per entity type via the `reltioIdScheme` setting in the tenant configuration.

Reltio IDs are stable across merges — when two entities merge, the surviving entity retains its Reltio ID.

parameters.name: reltioId
parameters.description: The Reltio ID of the entity.

200.description: The entity matching the specified Reltio ID.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified Reltio ID.

post.description:
Retrieves multiple entities by their URIs in a single request. This is more efficient than making individual GET requests when you need to fetch a known set of entities.

The request body contains an array of entity URIs. The response returns all found entities — URIs that don't match existing entities are silently skipped. Supports the same `options` query parameter as the single-entity GET for controlling response content.

200.description: The entities matching the specified URIs.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

get.description:
Retrieves the raw, uncompressed internal representation of an entity. Unlike the standard GET which returns the survivorship-resolved golden record, this endpoint returns the full internal storage structure including all crosswalk-level attribute values before survivorship resolution.

This is primarily a diagnostic/debugging endpoint used to understand why survivorship produced a particular golden record value, or to inspect the raw data contributed by each source system.

200.description: The raw entity representation with all crosswalk-level data.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified URI.

post.description:
Retrieves an entity profile with detailed survivorship rule evaluation results. In addition to the golden record values, the response includes which survivorship strategy was applied to each attribute and which source system's value was selected as the winner.

This endpoint is essential for building data stewardship UIs that need to explain *why* a particular value was chosen as the golden record value — e.g., "FirstName = 'John' was selected because the Recency strategy picked the most recently updated value from source CRM."

200.description: The entity profile with survivorship rule evaluation details.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

404.description: Not Found — no entity exists with the specified URI.

get.description:
Returns the total count of entities matching the specified filter criteria. Accepts the same `filter`, `q`, and `type` query parameters as the main entity search endpoint, but returns only the count instead of the full entity objects.

This is significantly faster than fetching all results when you only need to know how many entities match — for example, to display a search result count in the UI before fetching the first page, or to monitor data growth metrics.

200.description: The total count of matching entities.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

get.description:
Performs a batch search optimized for segmentation and analytics workflows. Unlike the standard search which returns full entity objects, this endpoint returns lightweight entity summaries suitable for building segment populations.

Used internally by Reltio's segmentation engine and externally by analytics integrations that need to identify entity populations matching specific criteria without downloading full profile data.

200.description: Entity summaries matching the segmentation criteria.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

post.description:
Batch search with key-based pagination — designed for iterating over large result sets without the performance degradation of deep offset-based pagination.

Unlike `GET /entities` with `offset`+`max` (which slows down as offset increases), `_scan` uses a cursor (`scrollId`) returned in each response to fetch the next page. This provides consistent performance regardless of how deep into the result set you are.

Typical use: export pipelines, data synchronization jobs, or any workflow that needs to process all entities matching a filter.

200.description: A page of entities with a scroll cursor for the next page.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

get.description: Returns the total count of entities for a batch search query. Companion endpoint to `POST /entities/v2/_scan` — use it to determine the total result size before starting a scan iteration.

200.description: The total count of matching entities.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

post.description:
Executes an advanced predicate-based query against entities or other object types. Predicate queries provide more expressive filtering than RQL — they support nested logical structures, complex attribute path navigation, and aggregate conditions.

The request body is a JSON predicate tree with operators like `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt`, `between`, `in`, `like`, `isNull`, combined via `and`, `or`, `not` logical operators.

The `objectType` path parameter specifies what to search: typically `entities` for entity search, but can also target `relations` or `interactions`.

200.description: Objects matching the predicate query.

400.description: Bad Request — invalid predicate structure or unknown attribute paths.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

post.description:
Cleanses entity data on-the-fly without persisting the result. Sends entity data through the tenant's configured cleansing rules and returns the cleansed output — useful for previewing cleansing results before committing data, or for client-side validation.

The entity is not stored in Reltio — this is a stateless transformation endpoint.

200.description: The cleansed entity data.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

post.description: Batch variant of the on-the-fly cleansing endpoint. Sends multiple entity records through the tenant's cleansing rules and returns all results in a single response. Useful for validating a batch of records before ingestion.

200.description: The batch of cleansed entity data.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token.

Entity.title: Entity Profile
Entity.description: A complete entity profile (golden record) as stored in Reltio. Represents a single real-world business object with all its attributes resolved by survivorship rules, crosswalks from contributing source systems, and operational metadata.

uri.description: The unique resource identifier for this entity. Format: `entities/{entityId}`. Generated by the platform on creation and immutable thereafter. Used in all API calls that reference this entity.

type.description: The entity type URI from the tenant configuration. Determines which attributes, match rules, and survivorship strategies apply to this entity. Format: `configuration/entityTypes/{TypeName}`.

tags.description: System and user-defined tags attached to the entity. Common system tags include `Suspect` (entity has unresolved potential matches), `ChangeRequest` (entity has pending change requests). Custom tags can be added via the API for workflow integration.

createdBy.description: The username or client ID of the authenticated caller who created this entity.

createdTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this entity was first created.

updatedBy.description: The username or client ID of the authenticated caller who last modified this entity.

updatedTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the most recent modification to this entity.

reltioId.description: A human-readable, auto-generated identifier unique within the tenant. Configurable per entity type via `reltioIdScheme` in the tenant configuration. Stable across merges.

isFavorite.description: Whether the current user has marked this entity as a favorite. Per-user flag, not stored on the entity itself.

label.description: The entity's display label, rendered from the `displayLabelPattern` configured on the entity type. Typically shows key identifying attributes (e.g., "John Smith" for a Person, "Acme Corp" for an Organization).

crosswalks.description: Source-specific record identifiers that link this entity to originating systems. Each crosswalk represents one source system's contribution to this entity. A merged entity has multiple crosswalks — one per source record that was merged into it.

attributes.description:
The entity's attribute values, organized as a map of attribute name to attribute value array. Each attribute can have multiple values (e.g., multiple phone numbers). The values shown are the golden record values — survivorship-resolved winners from all contributing crosswalks.

Attribute names correspond to the `uri` suffix of attribute definitions in the entity type configuration (e.g., if the config defines `configuration/entityTypes/Person/attributes/FirstName`, the key here is `FirstName`).

analyticsAttributes.description: System-computed analytics attributes such as merge counts, potential match counts, and data completeness scores. Read-only — populated automatically by the platform.

EntityInput.title: Entity Input
EntityInput.description: Request body for creating or updating an entity. Must include a type, at least one crosswalk, and the attribute values to set.

type.description: The entity type URI. Must reference a type defined in the tenant configuration.

crosswalks.description: Source system identifiers for this entity. At least one crosswalk is required on create to establish the source linkage.

attributes.description: Attribute values to set, organized as a map of attribute name to value array.

EntitySummary.title: Entity Summary
EntitySummary.description: A lightweight entity representation used in search results and batch operations. Contains the entity URI, type, key attributes, and operational metadata, but may omit full crosswalk details and nested attribute values.

attributes.description: Key attribute values for this entity.

createdTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this entity was created.

updatedTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last update.

Crosswalk.title: Crosswalk
Crosswalk.description: A source-specific record identifier that links a Reltio entity back to its originating system. Each crosswalk represents one source system's contribution and contains the source-level attribute values before survivorship resolution.

uri.description: The unique crosswalk URI within this entity.

type.description: The entity type URI this crosswalk belongs to.

value.description: The source system's record identifier value (e.g., CRM customer ID, ERP account number).

sourceTable.description: The source system name as defined in the tenant configuration's `sources` array.

createdTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this crosswalk was created.

updatedTime.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last update to this crosswalk.

attributes.description: The attribute values contributed by this source system, before survivorship resolution.

CrosswalkInput.title: Crosswalk Input
CrosswalkInput.description: Source identifier for linking an entity to an originating system.

sourceTable.description: The source system name from the tenant configuration.

AttributeValue.title: Attribute Value
AttributeValue.description: A single attribute value on an entity. Attributes can be simple (string, number, boolean) or nested (containing child attributes). Each value has an OV (original value — the raw input) and optionally a value (the cleansed/normalized form).

uri.description: Unique identifier for this attribute value within the entity.

type.description: The attribute type URI from the configuration.

ov.description: Original Value — the raw value as received from the source system, before any cleansing or normalization.

value.description: The current value of this attribute. For cleansed attributes, this is the normalized form. For non-cleansed attributes, this equals the OV.

AttributeValueInput.title: Attribute Value Input
AttributeValueInput.description: Input for setting an attribute value on an entity.

type.description: The attribute type URI (optional — inferred from attribute name if omitted).

EntityCreateResponse.title: Entity Create Response
EntityCreateResponse.description: Response from entity creation or Search Before Create operations.

uri.description: The URI of the created or updated entity.

object.description: The full entity object (included when `returnObjects=true` option is specified).

DeleteRequest.title: Delete Request
DeleteRequest.description: Request body for the POST-based entity deletion endpoint.

uris.description: Array of entity URIs to delete.

UriListRequest.title: URI List Request
UriListRequest.description: Request body for fetching multiple entities by URI.

uris.description: Array of entity URIs to retrieve.

TotalResponse.title: Total Count Response
TotalResponse.description: Response containing the total number of objects matching a query.

total.description: The total number of matching objects.

ScanRequest.title: Scan Request
ScanRequest.description: Request body for the key-based pagination scan endpoint.

scrollId.description: The cursor from a previous scan response. Omit on the first request to start from the beginning.

max.description: Maximum number of entities to return per page.

ScanResponse.title: Scan Response
ScanResponse.description: Response from the scan endpoint containing a page of entities and a cursor for the next page.

scrollId.description: Cursor to pass in the next request to get the next page. Null or absent when there are no more results.

PredicateQuery.title: Predicate Query
PredicateQuery.description: A structured predicate tree for advanced entity filtering. Supports nested logical operators and attribute-based conditions.

predicate.description: The root predicate node. Can be a logical operator (`and`, `or`, `not`) containing child predicates, or a leaf condition (`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt`, `between`, `in`, `like`, `isNull`) targeting a specific attribute path.

attributePath.description: The attribute path to evaluate (e.g., `attributes.FirstName.value`). Required for leaf conditions.

value.description: The comparison value. Type depends on the operator and attribute.

options.description: Query options like pagination and result shaping.
